_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 18 (three visitors + Sodom intercession). Saadia-specific moves: v.3 יא ולי אללה = 'O ally of God' (Saadia substitutes a respectful Arabic address for 'אדני', avoiding the divine-name reading); v.13 איקינא = 'verily' (Saadia's emphatic — Blau 3:1 documents this); v.21 'אורד אמרא מוגהא' = 'I shall send down a directed command' (= B11:5,7 — anti-anthropomorphic substitute for 'ארדה'); v.22 'יצלי' = 'praying' (Saadia adds explicit verb for Abraham's posture before God); v.25 אנת מעאד' = 'Far be it from You' (prayer-Arabic idiom for חלילה לך); v.33 'the light of God ascended' (anti-anthropomorphic).

translations.1: And God appeared to him in the plain of Mamre; and he was sitting at the door of the tent in the heat of the day.
translations.2: And he lifted up his eyes and saw — and behold, three men were standing before him. And when he saw them, he came to meet them from the door of the tent, and bowed down upon the earth.
translations.3: And he said: 'O ally of God! If I have found favor with you, do not pass by your servant.
translations.4: Let a little water be brought to you; and wash your feet; and lean under the tree.
translations.5: And I shall bring a piece of food, and stay your hearts; after that you may go on — for it is on this account that you have passed by your servant.' They said: 'Do as you have spoken.'
translations.6: And Abraham hastened to the tent, to Sarah, and said: 'Make haste — three measures of fine flour; knead it and make it into cake-bread.'
translations.7: And to the cattle Abraham hastened; and he took a calf, tender and good, and gave it to the youth; and he urged him to prepare it.
translations.8: And he took butter and milk, and the calf which he had prepared; and he set them before them; and he was standing before them under the tree; and they ate.
translations.9: And they said to him: 'Where is Sarah your wife?' And he said: 'Behold, she is in the tent.'
translations.10: He said: 'I shall return to you at this time of the coming year; and there shall be a son for Sarah your wife.' And Sarah was listening at the door of the tent, and it was behind her.
translations.11: And Abraham and Sarah had grown old, advanced in years; and it had ceased to be for Sarah the way of women.
translations.12: And Sarah laughed within herself, saying: 'After I have grown worn, shall I have splendor? And my lord is old.'
translations.13: And God said to Abraham: 'Why did Sarah laugh, saying, "Verily, shall I bear when I have grown old?"
translations.14: Is any matter hidden from God? At the appointed time I shall return to you at this time of the coming year — and Sarah shall have a son.'
translations.15: And Sarah denied, saying: 'I did not laugh' — for she was afraid. He said: 'No — but you did laugh.'
translations.16: Then the men rose from there, and looked out toward Sodom; and Abraham was going with them to escort them.
translations.17: And God said: 'Shall I hide from Abraham what I am doing —
translations.18: And Abraham — there shall come from him a great and mighty nation; and in him shall be blessed all the nations of the earth.
translations.19: And I know him — that he shall command his sons and his household after him, that they shall keep the way of God, to do righteousness and judgment — that God may bring upon Abraham what He has spoken concerning him.'
translations.20: And God said: 'The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has grown great; and their sin has grown exceedingly great.
translations.21: I shall send down a directed command, and I shall see: whether they have wholly done as their cry which has come to me — or not.'
translations.22: Then the men turned from there, and went toward Sodom; and Abraham was still standing — praying — before God.
translations.23: And Abraham drew near, and said: 'Will You verily sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
translations.24: Perhaps there are fifty righteous within the city — will You verily sweep them away, and not pardon the place for the sake of the fifty righteous who are in its midst?'
translations.25: Far be it from You — to do a thing of this kind — to destroy the righteous with the wicked, and that the righteous should be as the wicked! Far be it from You! Shall the Judge of all the world not deal justly?'
translations.26: God said: 'If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, I shall pardon all the dwellers of the place on their account.'
translations.27: And Abraham answered, and said: 'Behold, I have insistently spoken before God — and I am dust or ashes.
translations.28: Perhaps the fifty righteous shall lack five — will You destroy all the city because of the five?' He said: 'I shall not destroy them, if I find there forty-five.'
translations.29: And he repeated his speaking to Him, and said: 'Perhaps there shall be found there forty.' He said: 'I shall not do it, on account of the forty.'
translations.30: He said: 'Let it not be hard before God for me to speak; perhaps there shall be found there thirty.' He said: 'I shall not do it, if I find there thirty.'
translations.31: He said: 'Behold, I have insistently spoken before God; perhaps there shall be found there twenty.' He said: 'I shall not destroy them, on account of the twenty.'
translations.32: He said: 'Let it not be hard before God — and I shall speak this one time only; perhaps there shall be found there ten.' He said: 'I shall not destroy them, on account of the ten.'
translations.33: And the light of God ascended, when He had finished speaking with him; and Abraham returned to his place.
